explanation: Patting an adult's head in Italy isn't a strong taboo, but it can read as patronizing or overly familiar outside of close family or affectionate contexts with children. Italians are warm and tactile with people they know well, but unsolicited touching — especially to the head — can make someone uncomfortable if you're not close.
local_tip: Save head-pats for children or very close family, and stick to a handshake or light arm touch with everyone else.

also_check.note: The head is considered the most sacred body part in Thai culture, and touching it is a major taboo.
Patting an adult's head is generally seen as disrespectful, though it may be fine for close family or children.
A light pat can be friendly among close acquaintances but may feel overly familiar otherwise.
